notes:
Account background: ServeWorks runs a multi-tenant customer support SaaS (chat + KB search) with ~1.2k employees, heavy EU footprint. Initially on Redwood hosted API since 2023 for prototypes. Renewal/expansion trigger: support SLA complaints during Black Friday spikes — they want predictable latency and lower unit cost.

What they currently use: hosted API for chat generation and embeddings. Production traffic pattern: 08:00-20:00 local peaks, bursty in EU region.

Primary asks / requirements:
- Move to Dedicated capacity for stable p99 latency (<150ms per token) and throughput (sustained 12k tokens/s across region).
- EU data residency for user messages + embeddings; need contractual residency clause.
- KMS integration for key control and audit logging accessible in Console.
- SSO (SAML) + SCIM for team provisioning.
- Optimize adoption for batching/caching recommendations to reduce token costs by ~30%.

POC summary:
- 14-day Dedicated smoke test (NA+EU) completed 2026-02-24. Observations: autoscaling behaves well under steady load, KV prefix cache reduced token counts on FAQ flows by ~22%. Issue: occasional cold-start latency in EU when burst traffic routes to a warm pool in another AZ — SE investigating kernel selection for small sequence lengths.

Quote from CTO (2026-02-25 demo): "We need to be able to guarantee our customers a deterministic SLA — if Redwood can give predictable p99 and an easy path to EU residency, this scales across our enterprise customers."

Commercials & renewal:
- Current contract (hosted API) up for renewal 2026-06. We proposed Dedicated reserved capacity with a 12-month commitment and an Optimize add-on for workload tuning. Estimated ARR uplift $750k-$1.2M.

Risks & blockers:
- Legal: DPA/data residency language for EU not finalized (high).
- Finance: Wants staged payments + PO process (medium).
- Technical: Need confirmation on backup/restore SLA for Private option if they request on-prem DR (low-medium).
